Rows 7-23 show the donut shelves and a gray vertical divider face-on, and rows 24-29 are a front-facing base panel. No horizontal top surface is visible, and the width stays at 32 on every row from 0 to 30. The case therefore reads as a front elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a display case with a pale body, pink stripes and rows of donuts. It carries 19 visible tones per 16x16 tile, against 17 for the cheese stall and 20 for the roofed well, so it matches the richer references. Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no flat fills, and the white panels still show variation. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, which means the outline leans toward the material colour (brownish or pinkish) and does not read as a black sticker line. I count about 5 shading steps on the body and trim, slightly below the 5-6 on the references. The small donut clusters add texture, though the pale panels are somewhat simpler than the stall's wood grain and awning detail. Overall it holds up beside the references at the same scale.
